qualification: The published v0.4.8 client installed with the guide's one-line installer, signed in, bound to a project and connected to native Codex CLI 0.152.0 and GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.83 through `synveda adapter install`, then driven through their normal interactive trust prompts against a published v0.4.8 Docker evaluation server. macOS arm64 only; Linux and Windows were not run.

outcome.client_install: passed: publisher verified, 11 s, isolated install root and no shell-profile change
outcome.codex_registration: failed on a repository without .codex/hooks.json (`hooks` must be an object), including a reinstall after uninstall; passed once the file existed as {"hooks": {}}; fixed in source after v0.4.8
outcome.copilot_registration: passed: install, status, repeat, uninstall and reinstall
outcome.codex_live: passed for context, MCP recall, resume and delivery; tool calls were not recorded with gpt-5.6-luna
outcome.copilot_live: passed for context, MCP recall, tool recording and delivery; one session started after the sign-in expired and holds its events locally

host.server: published v0.4.8 reference bundle (source 5715df5f65789f66ba8010ad7a8b549673542e24) through its plain-Compose route, the retained 2026-11-04 sample installation brought back up in 214 s, with the fictional Northstar sample, its approved retry Knowledge and the Ingestion API project
host.account: synveda-demo-admin, whose password came from the bundle's deliberate credentials retrieval into a private file; the four demo accounts are synthetic
host.repository: a throwaway one-commit Git repository outside the product checkout

client_install.command: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/synveda/synveda/main/scripts/install.sh with SYNVEDA_VERSION=0.4.8, an isolated SYNVEDA_HOME and SYNVEDA_BIN, and SYNVEDA_NO_MODIFY_PATH=1
client_install.result: Release publisher verified for v0.4.8. Installed Synveda client 0.4.8 (darwin-arm64).

sign_in.route: synveda login --gateway http://localhost:8080: the gateway's PKCE flow against the bundled Keycloak, with a scripted HTTP user agent standing in for the browser (it had to send Keycloak's Secure cookies to http://localhost, as browsers do)
sign_in.expiry: the bundled realm refused the refresh token about five hours later; whoami then printed 'could not refresh the access token: the identity provider rejected the login; run `synveda login` again', and sign-in was repeated twice

setup.list: synveda setup listed one project: Ingestion API
setup.bind: synveda setup --project <Ingestion API> --observation on wrote .synveda/config.json with observe and managed_observation true

registration.dry_run: printed the hook file and `mcp add synveda -- <installed client>/bin/synveda mcp --writes host`
registration.fresh_repository: synveda: <repo>/.codex/hooks.json: `hooks` must be an object (exit 1); no file was written
registration.cause: strip_ours indexed document["hooks"] mutably on the empty document, which inserts null, so hooks_object refused it
registration.with_the_file: four hooks (SessionStart, PreCompact, Stop 12 s; SessionEnd 3 s) with absolute paths to the installed client's Node, hook and CLI; MCP server registered; status 'configured (receipt matches)'
registration.repeat: MCP already registered; hook file and Codex configuration unchanged
registration.uninstall: removed the hook file and the MCP entry
registration.reinstall_after_uninstall: failed with the same error, because uninstall removes the file it emptied
registration.unrelated_hooks: status still matched the receipt with three unrelated hooks added; uninstall removed only the Synveda entries

codex.trust: the project trust prompt, then /hooks: four new project hooks were trusted one by one; six hooks from already-enabled vendor plugins were left untrusted. /mcp listed synveda as connected with one tool.
codex.models: Codex 0.152.0 refused gpt-5.5 and the account's configured gpt-6.1-sol for a ChatGPT sign-in (400 model_not_found, before any model work); gpt-5.6-luna at low effort was used

turns.result: SessionStart context began 'Synveda Session ID: 01a1b719-9a09-7bb0-b141-96fd4eef24b0'; the answer echoed that ID and the approved retry rule (reuse the original Idempotency-Key; 409 while running; replay after completion)
synveda.recall({session_id, query: 'ingestion retry'}) returned 'Retry behaviour for ingestion requests'; no approval prompt
after exit, codex resume of the same conversation: SessionStart source resume returned the same Synveda Session ID
one more question answered from the context (409 while running); the Stop hook recorded nine entries covering all four turns

hook_log.session_start: session.opened and context.ok: 2 entries, 502 tokens, nothing degraded, 34-62 ms
hook_log.session_end: deliver.batch 9 events ok in 42 ms; turn.done acknowledged 9, pending 0, complete

codex.server: GET /v1/sessions/01a1b719-9a09-7bb0-b141-96fd4eef24b0: client_name codex, client_version 0.4.8, model_name gpt-5.6-luna, external_session_id codex:<native id>, status active; all nine events (four message.user, five message.assistant) appended on the first attempt
codex.tool_recording: with gpt-5.6-luna, Codex wrote both MCP calls as custom_tool_call items named exec (with custom_tool_call_output); the v0.4.8 transcript reader handles function_call only and skips these without a diagnostic, so no tool event was recorded
codex.usage: session 1 (turns 1-2): total 20,943 tokens (+47,616 cached), 270 output; resumed session (turns 3-4): total 1,340 (+40,704 cached), 54 output
operator_notes: An earlier attempt found no credentials because the sign-in had expired; signing in again fixed it. Turns 1-3 also ran with a scratch home that lacked the setup receipt managed observation requires, so their Stop hooks recorded nothing without a log line. Once the receipt was copied, turn 4's Stop read the whole transcript and recorded the nine entries. Both causes were the run's own environment.
codex mcp add rewrote the formatting of an existing [mcp_servers] table in the operator's Codex configuration (same values). That configuration was restored byte for byte after uninstall.

copilot.client: GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.83 (it downloaded 1.0.107 during the run; not applied)

registration.dry_run: printed .github/hooks/synveda.json and `mcp add synveda -- <installed client>/bin/synveda mcp --writes host`
registration.install: hook file version 1 with sessionStart, agentStop and sessionEnd, each running the installed client's Node and hook with SYNVEDA_CLI in env; MCP server in the user's Copilot configuration
registration.uninstall_and_reinstall: uninstall removed the hook file and the MCP entry; reinstall passed and status matched the receipt

copilot.trust: the folder trust prompt, answered for this session only; /mcp show listed synveda (user) enabled

turns.result: the sign-in had expired: the hook logged credentials.unavailable, the model reported no Synveda Session ID, and the turn's entries stayed in the local spool; 0.22 AI credits
after signing in again, a new conversation: Copilot Fusion chose gpt-6-luna; the answer echoed Synveda Session ID 01a1b862-58e2-7153-91db-5965818fd661 and the approved retry rule
Copilot first made an unrelated github-mcp-server call that failed, then asked approval for Synveda's 'Query governed Knowledge'; approved once, it returned 'Retry behaviour for ingestion requests'

hook_log.session_start: session.opened and context.ok: 2 entries, 502 tokens, nothing degraded, 40 ms
hook_log.session_end: deliver.batch 8 events ok in 56 ms; complete

copilot.server: GET /v1/sessions/01a1b862-58e2-7153-91db-5965818fd661: client_name copilot-cli, client_version 0.4.8, external_session_id copilot-cli:<native id>, status active; eight events appended: two message.user, two message.assistant, two tool.invoked and two tool.result
copilot.signed_out_session: the turn-1 conversation never opened a Synveda run; synveda session flush reported 'Delivered 0 event(s). 1 session(s) have no run opened yet.'
copilot.usage: 0.22 AI credits for the signed-out session and 0.29 for the second (71.0k input tokens, 52.7k cached; 257 output)
